--- a/inflection/__init__.py
+++ b/inflection/__init__.py
@@ -371,12 +371,55 @@ def titleize(word: str) -> str:
       >>> titleize("raiders_of_the_lost_ark")
       'Raiders Of The Lost Ark'
 
+    Words written in capitals, such as acronyms, are kept as they are::
+
+      >>> titleize("NASA rocket launch")
+      'NASA Rocket Launch'
+      >>> titleize("read the HTTP spec")
+      'Read The HTTP Spec'
+
+    If the whole string is written in capitals, there is no telling the
+    acronyms from the other words, so every word is capitalized::
+
+      >>> titleize("IN_PROGRESS")
+      'In Progress'
+
     """
+    word = _underscore_keeping_case(word)
+    if word.isupper():
+        word = word.lower()
+    # Strip a trailing "_id" (or "_ID") and turn underscores into spaces, as
+    # humanize() would, but without lower-casing the words.
+    word = re.sub(r"_[iI][dD]$", "", word).replace("_", " ")
     return re.sub(
+        r"\w+(?:'\w+)*",
+        lambda match: _titleize_word(match.group()),
+        word
+    )
+
+
+def _titleize_word(word: str) -> str:
+    """Capitalize a word for :func:`titleize`, keeping acronyms as they are."""
+    if _is_acronym(word):  # e.g. NASA, or a whole word like DON'T
+        return word
+    title = re.sub(
         r"\b('?\w)",
         lambda match: match.group(1).capitalize(),
-        humanize(underscore(word)).title()
+        word.lower().title()
     )
+    # Keep an acronym that is only a part of the word, as in NASA's.
+    return "'".join(
+        part if _is_acronym(part) else title_part
+        for part, title_part in zip(word.split("'"), title.split("'"))
+    )
+
+
+def _is_acronym(word: str) -> bool:
+    """
+    Tell whether the word is written in capitals, like NASA or MP3. A single
+    capital letter, like the A in "TheManWithoutAPast", is not an acronym.
+    """
+    return len(word) > 1 and word.isupper()

     word = re.sub(r"([A-Z]+)([A-Z][a-z])", r'\1_\2', word)
